notes: 1. SCOPE: This module is the Buyer Portal construction-linked Payment Schedule view at https://uat.xrportal.in/paymentschedule (Buyer host — NOT uat-web). It is a read-and-action screen: buyers VIEW milestones, amounts, due dates, paid/pending/overdue states; and ACTION a payment via the live gateway (FS Feature 1.2). Per-milestone the screen exposes a PAY action and a TRANSACTION DETAILS action.

2. AUTH: Buyer login is Mobile-OTP only (no password). UAT mobile = 8888888888, static UAT OTP = 147258 (BRD §4.2 / FRD Module 1). JWT is held in sessionStorage. Unauthenticated access to /paymentschedule redirects to '/' (visual-memory Route note).

3. PRECONDITIONS for a populated schedule: buyer must have a confirmed allocated unit (WINNER status) AND completed KYC — the schedule is generated post-KYC and unit confirmation (FS 1.3, FS 1.6 Rule 1, Milestone-Payments BRD §8 Rule 1). A buyer who booked but did not complete KYC has NO milestone schedule.

4. LIVE PAYMENT GATEWAY WARNING: any TC that performs a real pay/transact action hits the LIVE Easebuzz/Razorpay gateway on UAT. Such TCs are marked [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED], REQUIRE explicit user authorisation before execution, and MUST carry the ENV skip guard test.skip(process.env.ENV === 'uat', 'Skipped on UAT — live gateway'). Do NOT execute real-payment TCs unattended. View-only TCs (open page, select registration/unit, read milestones/amounts/due-dates/statuses, open empty state, view transaction details for already-paid rows) are SAFE.

5. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] = a disposable UAT record/state must be supplied before executing this test (e.g. a buyer with a triggered/demand-issued milestone, a buyer with a PARTIAL milestone, a buyer on a Time-linked or Down-payment plan, a buyer with a home-loan-linked milestone, a buyer with an early-bird discount, or live-gateway authorisation + test card).
6. [VERIFY WITH DEV] = behaviour not confirmed in BRD/FRD/FS/Workflow or not transcribed in visual-memory; confirm before treating Pass/Fail as authoritative.

7. PAYMENT STATUS GLOSSARY (Milestone-Payments BRD §5): pending = amount due, no payment made; partial = some payment received, balance remaining (totalPaid > 0 and < totalAmount); paid = full amount confirmed; VERIFICATION = payment received, under verification; PAID = confirmed and cleared. The Buyer-facing screen surfaces Pending / Partial / Paid (FS 1.4). 'Overdue' is NOT a documented Buyer-facing status — milestones become due when triggered; see DOC_DRIFT-002.

8. AMOUNT GLOSSARY: Total Amount = principal + GST + parking shown separately per milestone (FS 1.4, BRD §4.6 Rule 5, FRD Module 6); Already Paid = totalPaid so far; Outstanding / Total Outstanding = Total − Already Paid; Home-loan disbursement amount = bank tranche credited against a milestone (FIRST_DISBURSEMENT auto-credit, Milestone-Payments BRD §8 Rule 5); Early bird discount = discount applied if applicable (FS 1.4).

9. MILESTONE TYPES (Milestone-Payments BRD §3): BOOKING_AMOUNT, PERCENT (% of FAV), SDR (stamp duty + registration), AMOUNT (fixed flat), FIRST_DISBURSEMENT (first home-loan tranche), FIRST_DEMAND_PAYMENT. Amounts are FROZEN at schedule generation from the typology template (BRD §8 Rule 2) and do not change retroactively. Partial payments are allowed (BRD §8 Rule 3).

10. TABLE COLUMNS (visual-memory Key Structural Notes): MILESTONE | % DUE | GST | (blank — additional amount) | TOTAL AMOUNT | TOTAL OUTSTANDING | PAYMENT STATUS | PAY | TRANSACTION DETAILS. Selectors at top of page: REGISTRATION NO. dropdown (h5) and UNIT NO. dropdown (h5, dependent on registration). Table shows 'No data' until a registration + unit are selected/populated.

11. NOTIFICATIONS: buyer receives an SMS/WhatsApp when a milestone becomes due (FS How-to Note; Milestone-Payments How-to Step 1) — due notifications are dispatched via Kaleyra (WhatsApp) / Epinet (SMS) (BRD §8 Integrations). [FSD-CORRECTION] NO buyer notification is sent on milestone payment SUCCESS or FAILURE (BYR_PAY_FSD_028) — success/failure is silent by design; verify the backend side-effect, do not flag missing toast as a bug (CLAUDE.md Pipeline Discipline §6).
12. DOWNLOAD: [FSD-CORRECTION] schedule download/print is CLIENT-SIDE react-to-print only — there is NO server PDF endpoint and no server file stored (BYR_PAY_FSD_026).

13. RECONCILIATION & SOURCE-OF-TRUTH: the gateway webhook is the source of truth for payment status — a buyer who closes the browser mid-payment may still be marked paid (BRD §4.6 Rule 6). A reconciliation cron runs every 5 minutes to catch missed webhooks (Milestone-Payments BRD §8 Rule 7). Every confirmed milestone payment creates a Mavis milestone payment record and updates Mavis status (BRD §8 Rule 8). Status may take a moment to reflect after payment.

14. KNOWN BUG [BUG-REF: BUG-PAY-001] (BYR_PAY_FSD_027): on a gateway FAILURE callback the controller attempts MilestonePaymentTracking.status = 'FAILED', but the model ENUM allows only VERIFICATION / PAID (and the lifecycle statuses pending/partial/paid). MySQL throws 'Data truncated for column status'. Either the error is swallowed (inconsistent row) or it bubbles up. The Buyer-facing milestone correctly stays Pending on failure (BYR_PAY_023); the bug is backend-only.

15. DOC_DRIFT-001 — FS Feature 1.4 lists 'Already paid amount' and 'Outstanding balance' as separate fields, but the live table (visual-memory) surfaces TOTAL AMOUNT and TOTAL OUTSTANDING columns and a '% DUE' column not named in the FS field list. Live UI wins: TCs assert the on-screen column set (MILESTONE | % DUE | GST | TOTAL AMOUNT | TOTAL OUTSTANDING | PAYMENT STATUS | PAY | TRANSACTION DETAILS); 'Already Paid' is verified as a derived value (Total − Outstanding) or within Transaction Details.

16. DOC_DRIFT-002 — neither BRD/FRD/FS nor visual-memory documents an explicit 'Overdue' Buyer-facing status. The documented Buyer statuses are Pending / Partial / Paid only. An overdue/past-due milestone is treated as Pending-with-Pay-available. The single overdue-styling TC is flagged [VERIFY WITH DEV]; do not assert an 'Overdue' badge as authoritative until confirmed.

17. DOC_DRIFT-003 — FS 1.4 and the workflow reference 'due dates' / 'demand letters issued when a milestone becomes due', but visual-memory does NOT transcribe a DUE DATE column header (captured columns: MILESTONE | % DUE | GST | TOTAL AMOUNT | TOTAL OUTSTANDING | PAYMENT STATUS | PAY | TRANSACTION DETAILS). Due-date and demand-letter visibility TCs are flagged [VERIFY WITH DEV] pending confirmation of where on the live screen the due date / demand letter is exposed.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Payment Schedule page loads via direct URL
tcs.description: Verify that an authenticated buyer can open the Payment Schedule screen by navigating directly to /paymentschedule.
tcs.precond: A buyer is logged in (mobile 8888888888 / OTP 147258) with a valid session.
tcs.steps:
1. While logged in, go to https://uat.xrportal.in/paymentschedule.
2. Wait for the page to finish loading.
tcs.expected: The Payment Schedule page renders showing the 'Payment Schedule' heading, the REGISTRATION NO. and UNIT NO. dropdowns and the schedule area (table or 'No data' until a unit is selected).

tcs.scenario: To verify the schedule is accessible only post-KYC with WINNER status
tcs.description: Verify that the populated payment schedule is available only to a buyer whose unit is confirmed (WINNER) and whose KYC is complete.
tcs.precond: A buyer with a confirmed unit (WINNER) and completed KYC. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a WINNER + KYC-complete buyer.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as a WINNER + KYC-complete buyer.
2. Open /paymentschedule.
3. Select the registration and unit.
tcs.expected: The milestone schedule loads with milestone rows (schedule is generated post-KYC and unit confirmation — FS 1.3 / 1.6 Rule 1 / Milestone-Payments BRD §8 Rule 1).

tcs.scenario: To verify the schedule is reachable from the dashboard Pay > link
tcs.description: Verify that the buyer can reach the Payment Schedule from the Home Dashboard 'Pay >' link in the Payment Schedule column.
tcs.precond: A buyer is logged in and on the Home Dashboard with a booked registration showing a 'Pay >' link.
tcs.steps:
1. On the Home Dashboard, find the registration row's Payment Schedule column.
2. Click 'Pay >'.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] booked registration with a due milestone
tcs.expected: The buyer is taken to the Payment Schedule screen (FS How-to Step 1: from Home Dashboard click 'Pay >' next to a pending milestone).

tcs.scenario: To verify the schedule is reachable from Unit Details
tcs.description: Verify that the payment schedule breakdown is reachable from the Unit Details (allocated unit) screen.
tcs.precond: A buyer with a confirmed unit is on the Unit Details screen.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the allocated Unit Details screen.
2. Locate the Payment Schedule / milestone breakdown section.
tcs.expected: The milestone-by-milestone payment breakdown is shown within Unit Details (FRD Module 7 — PaymentSchedule detail). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm whether this is an inline section or a link to /paymentschedule.

tcs.scenario: To verify the side navigation is visible from Payment Schedule
tcs.description: Verify that the buyer navigation sidebar is present on the Payment Schedule screen.
tcs.precond: The buyer is on the Payment Schedule page.
tcs.steps:
1. Look at the navigation sidebar.
2. Note the listed items.
tcs.expected: The sidebar shows Home, Registration, Allotment, Homeloan, Project, Work Progress and Logout (visual-memory Navigation Sidebar).

tcs.scenario: To verify Logout from Payment Schedule ends the session
tcs.description: Verify that clicking Logout on the Payment Schedule screen clears the session and returns the buyer to login.
tcs.precond: The buyer is on the Payment Schedule page.
tcs.steps:
1. Click the Logout button in the sidebar.
2. Observe the redirect.
3. Try to return to /paymentschedule.
tcs.expected: The session is cleared (JWT removed from sessionStorage), the buyer is redirected to '/', and re-opening /paymentschedule redirects back to login.

tcs.description: Verify that the page heading text on the Payment Schedule screen reads 'Payment Schedule'.
tcs.precond: The buyer is on /paymentschedule.
tcs.steps: 1. Read the main heading at the top of the page.
tcs.expected: The heading (h2) reads exactly 'Payment Schedule' (visual-memory Page Heading).

tcs.scenario: To verify the REGISTRATION NO. label and dropdown render
tcs.description: Verify that the REGISTRATION NO. label and its selection dropdown are rendered on the screen.

tcs.steps: 1. Look below the heading for the REGISTRATION NO. control.
tcs.expected: A 'REGISTRATION NO.' label (h5) is shown with a dropdown to select a registration (visual-memory Registration/Unit Selectors).

tcs.scenario: To verify the UNIT NO. label and dropdown render

tcs.precond: The buyer is on /paymentschedule.
tcs.steps: 1. Look for the UNIT NO. control next to/after REGISTRATION NO.
tcs.expected: A 'UNIT NO.' label (h5) is shown with a dropdown to select a unit, dependent on the chosen registration (visual-memory Registration/Unit Selectors).

tcs.scenario: To verify the table column headers render in the correct order
tcs.description: Verify that the payment schedule table renders its column headers in the documented order.
tcs.precond: A registration and unit are selected so the table is populated. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a buyer with a populated schedule.
tcs.steps:
1. Select a registration and unit.
2. Read the table header row left to right.
tcs.expected: Headers appear in order: MILESTONE, % DUE, GST, (blank additional-amount column), TOTAL AMOUNT, TOTAL OUTSTANDING, PAYMENT STATUS, PAY, TRANSACTION DETAILS (visual-memory Payment Schedule Table).

tcs.scenario: To verify milestones are listed in chronological order
tcs.description: Verify that the milestone rows are displayed in chronological / construction-stage order.
tcs.precond: A populated schedule is loaded. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a multi-milestone schedule.
tcs.steps:
1. Select registration + unit to load the schedule.
2. Read the MILESTONE column top to bottom.
tcs.expected: Milestones are listed in order (all payment milestones in order — FS 1.4 / How-to Step 2), reflecting the construction-stage sequence.

tcs.scenario: To verify each milestone shows its trigger label
tcs.description: Verify that each milestone row shows what triggers the milestone (e.g., a construction stage).
tcs.precond: A populated schedule is loaded. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a multi-milestone schedule.
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule.
2. Read the MILESTONE label for each row.
tcs.expected: Each row shows the milestone/trigger label (e.g. 'Foundation completion') describing the construction stage that triggers it (FS How-to Step 2). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact trigger text format on the live row.

tcs.scenario: To verify the due date / demand letter is exposed per milestone
tcs.description: Verify where on the live row the milestone due date and/or demand-letter reference is shown.
tcs.precond: A populated schedule with at least one triggered milestone is loaded. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a triggered-milestone buyer.
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule.
2. Look for a due date and a demand-letter indicator on a triggered milestone row.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] FS 1.4 / 1.6 reference due dates and demand letters, but visual-memory does not transcribe a DUE DATE column (DOC_DRIFT-003). [To verify] confirm where the due date and demand-letter reference appear on the live row.

tcs.scenario: To verify the registration dropdown lists the buyer's registrations
tcs.description: Verify that the REGISTRATION NO. dropdown lists the registrations belonging to the logged-in buyer.
tcs.precond: A buyer with one or more registrations is on /paymentschedule. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a buyer with at least one registration.
tcs.steps:
1. Click the REGISTRATION NO. dropdown.
2. Read the listed options.
tcs.expected: The dropdown lists the buyer's own registration number(s) and no other buyer's records.

tcs.scenario: To verify selecting a registration populates the Unit dropdown
tcs.description: Verify that choosing a registration enables and populates the dependent UNIT NO. dropdown.
tcs.precond: The REGISTRATION NO. dropdown has at least one option. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a buyer with a confirmed unit.
tcs.steps:
1. Select a registration from REGISTRATION NO.
2. Open the UNIT NO. dropdown.
tcs.expected: After selecting the registration the UNIT NO. dropdown becomes enabled and lists the unit(s) tied to that registration (dependent dropdown — visual-memory).

tcs.scenario: To verify selecting registration + unit loads the schedule table
tcs.description: Verify that choosing both a registration and a unit loads the milestone schedule table.
tcs.precond: Both dropdowns have options. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] WINNER + KYC buyer.
tcs.steps:
1. Select a registration.
2. Select a unit.
3. Wait for the table to load.
tcs.expected: The payment schedule table loads with milestone rows for the selected unit, replacing the 'No data' empty state.

tcs.scenario: To verify changing the registration resets unit and table
tcs.description: Verify that changing the registration resets the unit selection and clears the previously loaded table.
tcs.precond: A registration + unit are selected and a table is shown. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a buyer with 2+ registrations.
tcs.steps:
1. With a schedule loaded, open REGISTRATION NO.
2. Select a different registration.
3. Observe the UNIT NO. dropdown and the table.
tcs.expected: The UNIT NO. selection is cleared/reset, the UNIT NO. options refresh for the new registration, and the table reverts to 'No data' until a new unit is chosen.

tcs.scenario: To verify a registration with no allocated unit gives an empty unit dropdown
tcs.description: Verify that selecting a registration that has no confirmed/allocated unit leaves the UNIT NO. dropdown empty and shows no schedule.
tcs.precond: A buyer has a registration without a confirmed unit. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a non-WINNER registration.
tcs.steps:
1. Select a registration that has no confirmed unit.
2. Open the UNIT NO. dropdown.
tcs.expected: The UNIT NO. dropdown is empty (no selectable unit) and the schedule area stays on the 'No data' empty state — no schedule exists pre-WINNER (FS 1.3).

tcs.scenario: To verify principal, GST and parking are shown separately
tcs.description: Verify that each milestone breaks out principal, GST and parking amounts as separate values.
tcs.precond: A populated schedule is loaded. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a buyer whose schedule includes parking.
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule.
2. Inspect a milestone row's amount breakdown.
tcs.expected: Principal, GST and parking are shown separately for the milestone (FS 1.4 / BRD §4.6 Rule 5 — GST broken out from principal; parking shown separately).

tcs.scenario: To verify GST is broken out separately in each row
tcs.description: Verify that the GST column shows GST distinct from the principal amount for each milestone row.
tcs.precond: A populated schedule is loaded. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] WINNER + KYC buyer.
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule.
2. Read the GST column for each row.
tcs.expected: Every row shows a distinct GST value separate from the principal (visual-memory GST column; BRD §4.6 Rule 5).

tcs.scenario: To verify Total Amount equals principal + GST + parking
tcs.description: Verify that the TOTAL AMOUNT for a milestone equals principal + GST + parking.
tcs.precond: A populated schedule with a row whose components are visible. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] WINNER + KYC buyer with parking.
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule.
2. Read the principal, GST and parking values for a row.
3. Read TOTAL AMOUNT for that row.
tcs.expected: TOTAL AMOUNT = principal + GST + parking (FS How-to Step 2; visual-memory TOTAL AMOUNT column).

tcs.scenario: To verify the Already Paid amount is shown accurately
tcs.description: Verify that the amount already paid for a milestone is shown and matches the payments made.
tcs.precond: A buyer with a PARTIAL or PAID milestone. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a buyer with a part-paid milestone.
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule for a unit with a part-paid milestone.
2. Read the already-paid value (derived as Total − Outstanding, or within Transaction Details).
tcs.expected: The already-paid amount equals totalPaid so far and reconciles with TOTAL AMOUNT minus TOTAL OUTSTANDING (DOC_DRIFT-001 — surfaced via Total/Outstanding or Transaction Details).

tcs.scenario: To verify Outstanding Balance equals Total minus Already Paid
tcs.description: Verify that the outstanding balance for a milestone equals Total Amount minus the amount already paid.
tcs.precond: A buyer with a PARTIAL milestone. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] partial-milestone buyer.
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule.
2. Read TOTAL AMOUNT and the already-paid amount for a partial row.
3. Read TOTAL OUTSTANDING.
tcs.expected: TOTAL OUTSTANDING = TOTAL AMOUNT − already-paid for that milestone.

tcs.scenario: To verify Total Outstanding reflects the unpaid balance per milestone
tcs.description: Verify that the TOTAL OUTSTANDING column reflects the remaining unpaid amount per milestone row.
tcs.precond: A populated schedule with pending and partial rows. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] mixed-status buyer.
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule.
2. Read TOTAL OUTSTANDING for a Pending row and a Partial row.
tcs.expected: TOTAL OUTSTANDING equals the full TOTAL AMOUNT for a Pending row, and the remaining balance for a Partial row, and shows zero / no value for a Paid row.

tcs.scenario: To verify the already-paid amount is surfaced for a Partial milestone
tcs.description: Verify that for a partially paid milestone the amount already paid is surfaced to the buyer.
tcs.precond: A buyer with a PARTIAL milestone. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] partial-milestone buyer.
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule.
2. Inspect the Partial milestone row and its Transaction Details.
tcs.expected: The already-paid portion is visible for the Partial milestone (status Partial means totalPaid > 0 and < totalAmount — BRD §5).

tcs.scenario: To verify the status badge shows 'Pending' for unpaid milestones
tcs.description: Verify that a milestone with no payment shows the Pending status.
tcs.precond: A buyer with at least one unpaid milestone. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] WINNER + KYC buyer.
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule.
2. Read the PAYMENT STATUS of an unpaid milestone.
tcs.expected: The PAYMENT STATUS shows 'Pending' for a milestone with no payment made (BRD §5 pending).

tcs.scenario: To verify the status badge shows 'Partial' when partially paid
tcs.description: Verify that a milestone with some payment but a remaining balance shows the Partial status.
tcs.precond: A buyer with a PARTIAL milestone. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] partial-milestone buyer.
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule.
2. Read the PAYMENT STATUS of a part-paid milestone.
tcs.expected: The PAYMENT STATUS shows 'Partial' (totalPaid > 0 and < totalAmount — BRD §5).

tcs.scenario: To verify the status badge shows 'Paid' when fully settled
tcs.description: Verify that a fully paid milestone shows the Paid status.
tcs.precond: A buyer with a fully PAID milestone. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] paid-milestone buyer.
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule.
2. Read the PAYMENT STATUS of a fully paid milestone.
tcs.expected: The PAYMENT STATUS shows 'Paid' once totalPaid >= totalAmount (BRD §5 paid).

tcs.scenario: To verify the Payment Status shows Pending / Partial / Paid
tcs.description: Verify that the PAYMENT STATUS column renders the correct one of Pending / Partial / Paid per milestone state.
tcs.precond: A buyer with milestones in all three states. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] mixed-status buyer.
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule.
2. Read the PAYMENT STATUS for a pending, a partial and a paid milestone.
tcs.expected: Each milestone shows exactly one of Pending / Partial / Paid matching its underlying state (FS 1.4).

tcs.scenario: To verify the schedule is generated per the selected payment plan
tcs.description: Verify that the milestone structure matches the buyer's selected payment plan type.
tcs.precond: A buyer whose payment plan type is known. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a buyer per plan type.
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule.
2. Compare the milestone structure to the buyer's selected plan (construction-linked / time-linked / down payment).
tcs.expected: The schedule milestones match the selected plan type chosen at registration (FS 1.5 — schedule generated from the selected plan).

tcs.scenario: To verify the home-loan disbursement amount shows per milestone
tcs.description: Verify that for a home-loan buyer the bank-disbursement amount is shown against the relevant milestone(s).
tcs.precond: A buyer with a home loan linked to the booking. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a home-loan buyer.
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule for a home-loan buyer.
2. Inspect milestones covered by bank disbursement.
tcs.expected: The amount disbursed by the bank at each relevant milestone is shown, distinguishing bank-covered milestones from buyer-paid ones (FS 1.4 / How-to Step 4; FIRST_DISBURSEMENT auto-credit — Milestone-Payments BRD §8 Rule 5).

tcs.scenario: To verify home-loan-linked milestone amount visibility
tcs.description: Verify that the schedule clearly distinguishes which milestones are covered by home-loan disbursement versus paid directly by the buyer.

2. Identify the home-loan-covered milestone and the buyer-paid milestones.

1. Load the schedule.

tcs.expected: PAY is absent or disabled for the non-triggered milestone — only triggered milestones are payable (FS 1.6 Rule 2/3).

tcs.scenario: To verify the Pay button is hidden after full payment
tcs.description: Verify that once a milestone is fully paid the PAY action no longer appears for it.
tcs.precond: A buyer with a fully PAID milestone. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] paid-milestone buyer.
tcs.steps:

2. Inspect the PAY column on the fully paid milestone.
tcs.expected: PAY is hidden/disabled for the fully paid milestone (status Paid).

tcs.scenario: To verify a Paid milestone hides/disables the PAY action
tcs.description: Verify that the PAY action is suppressed for a milestone in Paid status.
tcs.precond: A buyer with a paid milestone. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] paid-milestone buyer.
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule.
2. Confirm the PAY column shows no actionable Pay for the Paid milestone.
tcs.expected: No actionable PAY is shown for the Paid milestone; the row reflects a settled state.

tcs.scenario: To verify clicking Pay opens the Easebuzz gateway
tcs.description: Verify that clicking PAY on a due milestone opens the Easebuzz payment gateway.
tcs.precond: A buyer with a due milestone; live-gateway authorisation. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] gateway authorisation + due milestone — needs user authorisation; ENV skip guard test.skip(ENV==='uat').
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule.
2. Click PAY on a due milestone.
3. Observe the gateway opening.
tcs.expected: The Easebuzz payment gateway opens for the milestone amount (How-to Step 3 / FS 1.6 Rule 4). LIVE GATEWAY — requires user authorisation; do not run unattended; skip on UAT.

tcs.scenario: To verify clicking PAY initiates the payment gateway flow
tcs.description: Verify that the PAY action initiates the online payment gateway flow for the selected milestone.
tcs.precond: A buyer with a due milestone; live-gateway authorisation. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] gateway authorisation — needs user authorisation; ENV skip guard.
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule.
2. Click PAY on a due milestone.
3. Observe the gateway handoff.
tcs.expected: The payment gateway flow is initiated for the milestone (Easebuzz/Razorpay — BRD §8). LIVE GATEWAY — requires user authorisation; skip on UAT.

tcs.scenario: To verify the gateway shows the correct merchant
tcs.description: Verify that the opened payment gateway shows the correct merchant name.
tcs.precond: The Easebuzz gateway is open from a milestone Pay. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] live-gateway authorisation — needs user authorisation; ENV skip guard.
tcs.steps: 1. With the gateway open, read the merchant name field.
tcs.expected: Merchant = 'Impactum Lands Private Limited' (BRD §5 Phase 3 Step 6). LIVE GATEWAY — requires user authorisation; skip on UAT.

tcs.scenario: To verify all payment methods are listed in the gateway
tcs.description: Verify that the gateway lists the supported payment methods.
tcs.precond: The gateway is open from a milestone Pay. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] live-gateway authorisation — needs user authorisation; ENV skip guard.
tcs.steps: 1. With the gateway open, read the available payment methods.
tcs.expected: The gateway lists Credit Card, Debit Card, UPI, NetBanking and Wallets (BRD §5 Phase 3 Step 6). LIVE GATEWAY — requires user authorisation; skip on UAT.

tcs.scenario: To verify a successful payment updates the milestone to Paid
tcs.description: Verify that a successful gateway payment moves the milestone status to Paid (or Partial for a part-payment).
tcs.precond: A due milestone and a completed test payment; live-gateway authorisation. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] gateway authorisation + test card — needs user authorisation; ENV skip guard.
tcs.steps:
1. Pay a due milestone fully via the gateway.
2. Return to /paymentschedule.
3. Read the milestone status.
tcs.expected: After webhook confirmation the milestone PAYMENT STATUS becomes Paid (or Partial for a part-payment); webhook is source of truth so status may take a moment (BRD §4.6 Rule 6; Milestone-Payments §4). LIVE GATEWAY — requires user authorisation; skip on UAT.

tcs.scenario: To verify a buyer can pay a milestone in multiple tranches
tcs.description: Verify that a buyer may pay part of a milestone, leaving the status Partial with a remaining balance.
tcs.precond: A due milestone allowing partial payment; live-gateway authorisation. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] gateway authorisation — needs user authorisation; ENV skip guard.
tcs.steps:
1. Pay less than the full TOTAL OUTSTANDING for a due milestone.
2. Return to /paymentschedule.
3. Read the status and outstanding balance.
tcs.expected: Status moves to Partial, Already Paid increases by the tranche and TOTAL OUTSTANDING reduces accordingly (partial payments allowed — BRD §8 Rule 3; How-to 'Partial payments are accepted'). LIVE GATEWAY — requires user authorisation; skip on UAT.

tcs.scenario: To verify paying the remaining balance moves a Partial milestone to Paid
tcs.description: Verify that paying the remaining outstanding on a Partial milestone clears it to Paid.
tcs.precond: A Partial milestone with a remaining balance; live-gateway authorisation. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] partial milestone + gateway authorisation — needs user authorisation; ENV skip guard.
tcs.steps:
1. On a Partial milestone, pay the remaining TOTAL OUTSTANDING.
2. Return to /paymentschedule.
3. Read the status.
tcs.expected: Once totalPaid >= totalAmount the status becomes Paid and TOTAL OUTSTANDING is cleared (BRD §5 / §8 Rule 3). LIVE GATEWAY — requires user authorisation; skip on UAT.

tcs.scenario: To verify Transaction Details opens for a Paid/Partial milestone
tcs.description: Verify that the TRANSACTION DETAILS action opens the payment history for a Paid or Partial milestone.
tcs.precond: A buyer with a Paid or Partial milestone. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] paid/partial-milestone buyer.
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule.
2. Click TRANSACTION DETAILS on a Paid/Partial milestone.
tcs.expected: Transaction details for the milestone open, showing the recorded payment(s) (amount, date, reference). View-only — safe.

tcs.scenario: To verify Transaction Details for an unpaid (Pending) milestone
tcs.description: Verify how TRANSACTION DETAILS behaves for a milestone with no payments.
tcs.precond: A buyer with a Pending milestone. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] pending-milestone buyer.
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule.
2. Click/inspect TRANSACTION DETAILS on a Pending milestone.
tcs.expected: No transactions are shown for the Pending milestone — the action is empty/disabled or shows a 'no transactions' state (negative-path display).

tcs.scenario: To verify the demand letter is accessible per milestone
tcs.description: Verify that the demand letter for a triggered milestone is accessible from the schedule.
tcs.precond: A buyer with a triggered milestone (demand letter generated). [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] triggered-milestone buyer.
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule.
2. Locate and open the demand letter for the triggered milestone.
tcs.expected: The demand letter generated when the milestone became due is accessible (FS 1.6 Rule 3 — demand letters generated when a milestone becomes due). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm where the demand letter is exposed on the live row (DOC_DRIFT-003).

tcs.scenario: To verify schedule download is client-side react-to-print only
tcs.description: Verify the documented design that downloading/printing the schedule is client-side react-to-print with no server PDF endpoint.
tcs.precond: The buyer is on the Payment Schedule page.
tcs.steps:
1. Click 'Download' / 'Print Schedule'.
2. In DevTools Network, confirm there is NO server GET to a /pdf or /download-schedule endpoint.
3. Confirm the browser print dialog opens.
tcs.expected: [FSD-CORRECTION] The browser print dialog opens via react-to-print; no server PDF is generated and no server file is stored — documented as expected design (BYR_PAY_FSD_026).

tcs.scenario: To verify the 'No data' empty state shows when no selection is made
tcs.description: Verify that before a registration + unit are selected the schedule area shows the 'No data' empty state.
tcs.precond: The buyer is on /paymentschedule with nothing selected.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /paymentschedule.
2. Do not select a registration/unit.
3. Observe the schedule area.
tcs.expected: The table shows the 'No data' empty state (visual-memory Empty State — shown when no unit selected or no payment data).

tcs.scenario: To verify a buyer with no WINNER registration sees no schedule
tcs.description: Verify that a buyer without any confirmed/WINNER registration has no payment schedule to view.
tcs.precond: A buyer with only non-WINNER registrations. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a non-WINNER buyer.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as a buyer with no WINNER registration.
2. Open /paymentschedule.
3. Try to select a registration/unit.
tcs.expected: No populated schedule is available; the 'No data' empty state persists (schedule exists only post-WINNER + KYC — FS 1.3).

tcs.scenario: To verify a booked-but-no-KYC buyer has no milestone schedule
tcs.description: Verify that a buyer who booked (WINNER) but has not completed KYC sees no milestone schedule.
tcs.precond: A WINNER buyer who has NOT completed KYC. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a WINNER-without-KYC buyer.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as a WINNER buyer without completed KYC.
2. Open /paymentschedule and select the registration/unit.
tcs.expected: No milestone schedule is shown — the schedule is generated only after KYC submission (Milestone-Payments BRD §8 Rule 1: 'a buyer who booked but did not complete KYC has no milestone schedule').

tcs.scenario: To verify unauthenticated access redirects to login
tcs.description: Verify that opening /paymentschedule without a session redirects to the buyer login.
tcs.precond: No active buyer session (sessionStorage cleared).
tcs.steps:
1. Clear the session / open a fresh browser.
2. Navigate directly to https://uat.xrportal.in/paymentschedule.
tcs.expected: The buyer is redirected to '/' (login); the schedule is not exposed (visual-memory Route — unauthenticated access redirects to '/').

tcs.scenario: To verify a failed payment leaves the milestone Pending
tcs.description: Verify that a gateway FAILURE leaves the milestone status as Pending with a retry path.
tcs.precond: A due milestone; a forced gateway failure. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] gateway authorisation + forced failure — needs user authorisation; ENV skip guard.
tcs.steps:
1. Click PAY on a due milestone.
2. Force the gateway to return FAILURE.
3. Return to /paymentschedule and read the status.
tcs.expected: The milestone status stays Pending, an error toast is shown and retry is possible (unit/milestone is not advanced on failure). LIVE GATEWAY — requires user authorisation; skip on UAT.

tcs.scenario: To verify a backend 500 on schedule load shows a friendly error
tcs.description: Verify that a server error while loading the schedule shows a user-friendly error rather than a raw failure.
tcs.precond: The buyer is on /paymentschedule; the schedule API can be forced to 500.
tcs.steps:
1. Force the schedule-load API to return 500 (DevTools block/override).
2. Select a registration + unit.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] BRD §11 states network errors show user-friendly messages and session expiry prompts re-login. [To verify] confirm the exact on-screen error string and that the page does not crash.

tcs.scenario: To verify a due-milestone notification is dispatched to the buyer
tcs.description: Verify that when a milestone becomes due the buyer receives an SMS/WhatsApp notification to pay.
tcs.precond: A milestone is triggered for the buyer; message-log visibility. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] message-log access + a milestone trigger.
tcs.steps:
1. Trigger a milestone (admin-side) for the buyer.
2. Check the buyer's outbound message log.
tcs.expected: The buyer receives a due notification (SMS via Epinet / WhatsApp via Kaleyra) prompting payment (FS How-to Note; Milestone-Payments How-to Step 1). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the channel and template.

tcs.scenario: To verify no buyer notification on milestone payment success or failure
tcs.description: Verify the documented design that no buyer notification is sent on milestone payment success or failure (silent by design).
tcs.precond: A milestone payment completes (success or failure); message-log visibility. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] message-log access + completed payment.
tcs.steps:
1. Complete a milestone payment (success), then a failed one.
2. Check the buyer's outbound message log around each event.
tcs.expected: [FSD-CORRECTION] No SMS/WhatsApp/email is dispatched to the buyer on milestone payment success OR failure (silent by design — BYR_PAY_FSD_028). Silence is the REQUIRED assertion; verify backend side-effect, do not flag as a bug (CLAUDE.md §6).

tcs.scenario: To verify a confirmed milestone payment creates a Mavis record
tcs.description: Verify that a confirmed milestone payment creates a Mavis milestone payment record and updates Mavis status.
tcs.precond: A confirmed milestone payment; Mavis record visibility. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] Mavis access + a confirmed payment.
tcs.steps:
1. Complete a milestone payment (webhook-confirmed).
2. Inspect the Mavis milestone payment records and status.
tcs.expected: A Mavis milestone payment record is created and the Mavis milestone status is updated (Milestone-Payments BRD §8 Rule 8). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the Mavis record fields.

tcs.scenario: To verify the reconciliation cron catches a missed webhook
tcs.description: Verify that a milestone payment whose gateway webhook was missed is reconciled by the 5-minute cron.
tcs.precond: A milestone payment whose webhook is suppressed; backend visibility. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] backend access + ability to suppress the webhook.
tcs.steps:
1. Complete a milestone payment but suppress the gateway webhook.
2. Wait for the reconciliation cron (runs every 5 minutes).
3. Re-check the milestone status.
tcs.expected: After the cron runs the milestone status reflects the actual payment (reconciliation cron catches missed webhooks — Milestone-Payments BRD §8 Rule 7). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the cron interval/behaviour on UAT.

tcs.scenario: To verify webhook is source of truth if the buyer closes the browser mid-payment
tcs.description: Verify that a buyer who closes the browser mid-payment is still marked paid once the webhook confirms.
tcs.precond: A due milestone; live-gateway authorisation. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] gateway authorisation — needs user authorisation; ENV skip guard.
tcs.steps:
1. Start a milestone payment via the gateway.
2. After submitting payment, close the browser before the success redirect.
3. Re-open /paymentschedule and read the milestone status.
tcs.expected: The milestone is marked Paid once the gateway webhook confirms — status is driven by the webhook, not the browser (BRD §4.6 Rule 6). LIVE GATEWAY — requires user authorisation; skip on UAT.

tcs.scenario: To verify the schedule API returns the milestone list for a WINNER+KYC buyer
tcs.description: Verify that the payment-schedule API returns the milestone records for an authorised WINNER+KYC buyer's unit.
tcs.precond: An API client with a valid buyer JWT. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access + WINNER+KYC buyer token.
tcs.steps:
1. Call the payment-schedule endpoint with the buyer JWT and the registration/unit.
2. Read the HTTP status and body.
tcs.expected: HTTP 200 with the milestone list (milestone, % due, GST, total amount, outstanding, status per milestone). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact endpoint path and response shape (not transcribed in visual-memory).

tcs.scenario: To verify the schedule API rejects an unauthenticated request
tcs.description: Verify that calling the payment-schedule API without a valid token is rejected.
tcs.precond: An API client with no/invalid token. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Call the payment-schedule endpoint with no Authorization header.
2. Call again with a tampered token.
tcs.expected: The endpoint returns 401/403 and exposes no schedule data (auth gate). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact status code.

tcs.scenario: To verify a buyer cannot read another buyer's schedule (tenant isolation)
tcs.description: Verify that a buyer JWT cannot retrieve a registration/unit that belongs to a different buyer.
tcs.precond: An API client with buyer A's JWT and buyer B's registration/unit id. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access + two buyers' identifiers.
tcs.steps:
1. Authenticate as buyer A.
2. Call the payment-schedule endpoint with buyer B's registration/unit id.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] buyer A JWT + buyer B registration/unit
tcs.expected: The request is rejected / returns no data (403 or empty) — a buyer can only read their own schedule. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the isolation enforcement and status code.

tcs.scenario: To verify the milestone status FAILED is unsupported by the model
tcs.description: Verify the documented bug that a FAILED status write triggers a DB truncation because the model ENUM does not include FAILED.
tcs.precond: A milestone payment with a forced gateway-failure callback; backend/DB visibility. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] backend + DB access; forced failure.
tcs.steps:
1. Initiate an online payment for an outstanding milestone.
2. Force the Easebuzz failure callback.
3. Inspect the DB and backend logs.
tcs.expected: [BUG-REF: BUG-PAY-001] The controller attempts MilestonePaymentTracking.status = 'FAILED' but the model ENUM allows only VERIFICATION / PAID (and lifecycle pending/partial/paid). MySQL throws 'Data truncated for column status'. Either the error is swallowed (inconsistent row) or it bubbles up. Document the bug; the Buyer-facing milestone correctly stays Pending (BYR_PAY_023).

tcs.scenario: To verify one MilestonePaymentTracking record per milestone at schedule generation
tcs.description: Verify that schedule generation creates one MilestonePaymentTracking row per milestone, all starting pending with totalPaid = 0.
tcs.precond: A buyer whose schedule was just generated post-KYC; DB access. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] DB access + a freshly-KYC'd buyer.
tcs.steps:
1. Complete KYC for a WINNER buyer (or use a freshly generated schedule).
2. Query MilestonePaymentTracking for that registration/unit.
tcs.expected: One row exists per milestone, each with status = pending and totalPaid = 0 (Milestone-Payments BRD §4 lifecycle). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the table/columns.

tcs.scenario: To verify amounts are frozen at schedule generation
tcs.description: Verify that a milestone's totalAmount does not change retroactively after a later template (versionId) update.
tcs.precond: A buyer with a generated schedule; admin updates the milestone template afterwards; DB access. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] DB access + template-version change.
tcs.steps:
1. Record the milestone totalAmount values for the buyer.
2. Have admin update the milestone template (new versionId).
3. Re-query the buyer's milestone amounts.
tcs.expected: The buyer's existing milestone totalAmount values are unchanged — amounts are frozen at generation and template updates do not affect existing schedules (BRD §8 Rules 2 & 4).

tcs.scenario: To verify milestone records are soft-deleted on booking cancellation
tcs.description: Verify that cancelling a booking soft-deletes the milestone records rather than hard-deleting them.
tcs.precond: A buyer with a generated schedule whose booking is then cancelled; DB access. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] DB access + a cancellable booking.
tcs.steps:
1. Record the buyer's milestone rows.
2. Cancel the booking (admin-side).
3. Query MilestonePaymentTracking including soft-deleted rows.
tcs.expected: The milestone rows are soft-deleted (deletedAt set), not hard-deleted — the audit trail is preserved (BRD §8 Rule 6). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the soft-delete column.

tcs.scenario: To verify the real-payment path is skipped on the live UAT gateway
tcs.description: Verify that any TC performing a real payment is skipped in automation on UAT to avoid hitting the live gateway.
tcs.precond: ENV = uat.
tcs.steps: 1. Attempt a real payment on UAT in an automated run.
tcs.expected: The test is marked skipped in automation via test.skip(process.env.ENV === 'uat', 'Skipped on UAT — live gateway') — no real payment is executed unattended.

tcs.scenario: To verify an overdue (past-due) milestone is still payable as Pending
tcs.description: Verify how a milestone that is past its due date is presented and that it remains payable.
tcs.precond: A buyer with a triggered milestone past its due date. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] an overdue-milestone buyer.
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule for a buyer with a past-due triggered milestone.
2. Read the PAYMENT STATUS and PAY availability for that milestone.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] No 'Overdue' status is documented (DOC_DRIFT-002) — the milestone is expected to show Pending with PAY still available. [To verify] confirm whether the live UI applies any overdue styling/label.

tcs.scenario: To verify the final handover milestone behaves like other milestones
tcs.description: Verify that the final (handover) milestone is shown and payable like the preceding milestones until cleared.
tcs.precond: A buyer whose schedule includes a final handover milestone. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a near-complete-schedule buyer.
tcs.steps:
1. Load the schedule.
2. Inspect the final milestone row's amount, status and PAY.
tcs.expected: The final handover milestone is shown with its amount and status and is payable when triggered; once paid, the cycle is complete (Milestone-Payments BRD §4 — cycle repeats until final handover milestone paid).

tcs.scenario: To verify the end-to-end pay-one-milestone journey (gateway success path)
tcs.description: Verify the full journey: open the schedule, select registration and unit, pay one due milestone via the gateway, and see the status update.
tcs.precond: A buyer with a due milestone and PAY available; live-gateway authorisation. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] gateway authorisation + test creds — needs user authorisation; ENV skip guard test.skip(ENV==='uat').
tcs.steps:
1. Open /paymentschedule.
2. Select the registration.
3. Select the unit.
4. Click PAY on the due milestone.
5. Complete the gateway with test credentials.
6. Return to /paymentschedule.
tcs.expected: The row's PAYMENT STATUS updates to Paid (or Partial for a part-payment), TOTAL OUTSTANDING reduces and TRANSACTION DETAILS now shows the new entry. Webhook is source of truth so the status may take a moment to reflect (BRD §4.6 Rule 6). LIVE GATEWAY — requires user authorisation; do not run unattended; skip on UAT.
